record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: For every Hilbert-space dimension d, does there exist a SIC-POVM that is covariant under the d-dimensional Heisenberg, Weyl-Heisenberg, or generalized Pauli group? Equivalently, does there always exist a fiducial vector phi such that the orbit of |phi><phi| under all Weyl operators w(p,q) induces a SIC-POVM?

evidence.quote:
A vector |φi is called a fiducial vector with respect to the Heisenberg group if the set
{w(p, q)|φihφ| w(p, q)∗}p,q=0...d−1
induces a SIC-POVM. Such a SIC-POVM is said to be group covariant.
The problem: decide if group covariant SIC-POVMs exist in any dimension d.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 2$ be a positive integer and let $\mathcal{H}=\mathbb{C}^d$. Fix a basis $\{|0\rangle,\ldots,|d-1\rangle\}$ and set $\omega=e^{2\pi i/d}$. Define the Weyl (generalized Pauli) operators on $\mathcal{H}$ by
$$X|k\rangle=|k+1\bmod d\rangle,\qquad Z|k\rangle=\omega^{k}|k\rangle,\qquad w(p,q)=\tau^{pq}X^{p}Z^{q},$$
where $\tau=-e^{i\pi/d}$ (so that $\tau^2=\omega$), for $p,q\in\{0,1,\ldots,d-1\}$. The group generated by these operators is the (finite) Heisenberg–Weyl group in dimension $d$.

A symmetric informationally complete positive operator-valued measure (SIC-POVM) on $\mathcal{H}$ is a collection of $d^{2}$ rank-one operators $\frac{1}{d}|\psi_{j}\rangle\langle\psi_{j}|$, $j=1,\ldots,d^{2}$, where each $|\psi_{j}\rangle\in\mathcal{H}$ is a unit vector, $\sum_{j} \frac{1}{d}|\psi_{j}\rangle\langle\psi_{j}|=I$, and
$$|\langle\psi_{j}|\psi_{k}\rangle|^{2}=\frac{1}{d+1}\quad\text{for all } j\neq k.$$

A unit vector $|\varphi\rangle\in\mathcal{H}$ is called a fiducial vector (with respect to the Heisenberg–Weyl group) if the $d^{2}$ operators
$$\bigl\{w(p,q)\,|\varphi\rangle\langle\varphi|\,w(p,q)^{*}\bigr\}_{p,q=0,\ldots,d-1}$$
together with the normalization $1/d$ form a SIC-POVM. Such a SIC-POVM is called group-covariant.

Question: Does a Heisenberg–Weyl group covariant SIC-POVM exist for every dimension $d\ge 2$? Equivalently, does there exist a fiducial vector $|\varphi\rangle\in\mathbb{C}^{d}$ for every $d\ge 2$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is known as Zauner's conjecture. As of 2025, no general proof has been established. Numerical fiducial vectors are known in all dimensions up to about d=151 (and many others up to d≈844), and exact algebraic solutions have been obtained in many dimensions, with recent constructions via Stark units extending the list of exact cases (e.g., d=28, 52, 124, and certain prime-power forms). A constructive approach reduces existence in all dimensions to (still-unproven) cases of Stark's conjecture together with a special-value identity. Thus the problem remains open in general, with substantial partial progress.
